verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED on five independent grounds.

(1) NOTHING IS MISSING. The kind label 'missing-heading' is factually wrong. All three headings are present in specs/ISO_COBOL.md with text matching the printed page verbatim, in the correct order, each followed by its correct body: line 46567 '## D.19.11.1 General', line 46572 '## D.19.11.2 Main program', line 46595 '## D.19.11.3 Account class'. The surrounding content is also intact and correct -- the BANKMAIN program listing, the 'CLASS-ID. Account INHERITS Base.' listing, the three-factory-method bullet list and the five-instance-method bullet list all match the render character-for-character. Not one word of page 1156 is absent.

(2) THE PDF ENCODES NO HEADING LEVEL TO LOSE. I rendered both pages at 300 dpi and looked at the printed glyphs. 'D.19.11  Sample application' at the foot of p.1155 and 'D.19.11.1  General' at the head of p.1156 are set in the IDENTICAL bold serif face, at the IDENTICAL point size, at the IDENTICAL left margin, with the IDENTICAL number-to-title tab stop. ISO does not typographically distinguish clause depth anywhere in Annex D. In the source document the hierarchy is carried EXCLUSIVELY by the dotted clause number -- and that number is preserved character-for-character in the markdown heading text. The transcription therefore loses nothing the PDF actually expresses; the claim asks the markdown to add a distinction the canonical source does not make.

(3) THE HIERARCHY IS FULLY PRESENT AND MACHINE-RECOVERABLE. 'D.19.11.1' is unambiguously a subclause of 'D.19.11' by its own number. Any consumer that needs the outline parses the number, which is intact; the generated anchors encode it too (section-d-19-11, section-d-19-11-1, -2, -3). The assertion that 'the outline of the whole sample-application group is lost' is false -- the outline is recoverable by inspection from the text that is on the page.

(4) THE CLAIM'S CENTRAL PREMISE IS FALSIFIED BY THE DOCUMENT ITSELF. The claim assumes '#' count is a load-bearing hierarchy carrier in this transcription. It is not, anywhere. Measured across the whole spec, clause-depth-4 headings appear at md-h3 668 times, at md-h2 241 times and at md-h4 32 times; clause-depth-3 headings split 532 at md-h3 versus 337 at md-h2; clause-depth-5 splits 151/144/43 across h3/h2/h4. Marker depth and clause depth are globally uncorrelated. Parent and child sitting at the same marker level is the pervasive norm, not a local defect: '## Annex D' is immediately followed by its own child '## Concepts'; '## D.19 Object oriented concepts' (line 45609) has child '## D.19.3 Objects' (line 45637) at the very same '##'; '## D.19.5.4.2 Class polymorphism' is a depth-5 clause at '##'. These three headings are three instances out of 241+ of a uniform document-wide convention.

(5) THERE IS NO LOCALIZED 'FLATTENING ARTIFACT' AND NO 'FIRST SUBCLAUSE' RULE TO VIOLATE. The claim escalates on the theory that the first subclause normally retains a deeper marker and was exceptionally flattened here. No such rule exists: D.19.4.3, D.19.5.3, D.19.7, D.19.8, D.19.9.3 and D.19.10 all sit at '##', while D.19.3.1 and D.19.3.2 sit at '###' and their sibling D.19.3.3 sits at '##'. The pattern is arbitrary throughout, so pages 1150 and 1156 are not evidence of a systemic artifact -- they are ordinary samples of a convention that never encoded depth.

This is a markup/formatting difference in a presentational layer the source does not specify, with zero effect on meaning. Annex D is additionally marked '(informative)', so no normative syntax, general rule or semantic statement is touched. Per the rejection criteria -- text actually present, difference is formatting only, meaning unchanged -- the finding is rejected.
verdict.corrected_description: No discrepancy. All three headings (D.19.11.1 General, D.19.11.2 Main program, D.19.11.3 Account class) are present in the markdown with verbatim-correct text, correct order and correct body content, as is the rest of page 1156. The only difference is the markdown '#' count, which the PDF does not specify: ISO sets D.19.11 and D.19.11.1 in identical typography, carrying depth solely through the dotted clause number, which the transcription preserves exactly. Marker depth is uncorrelated with clause depth throughout the entire document (241 depth-4 clauses sit at '##'; even '## Annex D' is followed directly by its child '## Concepts', and '## D.19' by its child '## D.19.3'), so this is a document-wide presentational convention rather than a page-1156 defect. If the project wants markdown nesting to mirror clause numbering, that is a global, mechanical, purely cosmetic re-leveling task driven off the clause numbers already present -- not a per-page content discrepancy, and it should be tracked as a single formatting item rather than ledgered page by page as lost content.
